findings.message: Figure/prose transposition in topic-01.mdx. Lines 47-50 introduce the five scope areas with "The table below shows each area with one question a teacher in Sindh might actually ask", but the <Figure> carrier at line 50 is fig-U1-1 (four-spheres diagram; SVG text confirmed: "Planet Earth's four spheres"). The scope table fig-U1-2 ("What environmental science studies: five scope areas") is carried at line 87, inside the Earth-structure section, with no introducing prose. A learner is directed to a table that is not there, and the diagram that illustrates the four spheres never appears beside the spheres explanation. Verified in the rendered page (renders/desktop-topic-01.png). Repair: swap the two carriers in docs/semester-1/gnas-301/unit-01/topic-01.mdx so fig-U1-2 follows the scope sentence at line 47-48 and fig-U1-1 sits in the four-spheres section (around line 80); the figure manifest rows and gates are position-independent, so no other file changes.

Unbound citation for the 99% air-quality claim. topic-01.mdx:55-57 cites "(WHO, 2024)" for "almost the whole world's population, 99 per cent, breathes air that exceeds its guideline levels". The figure is real (WHO Ambient (outdoor) air pollution fact sheet, 24 Oct 2024: "In 2019, 99% of the world's population was living in places where the WHO air quality guidelines levels were not met", verified by direct fetch 2026-09-23), but no 2024 WHO source is bound: sources/unit-01.md carries only who-biodiversity-2025, who-climate-2023, un-restoration, abbas2012, archer2012, archer2010 plus the two flagged monographs, and no bound excerpt states this figure. This breaks the unit's own contract (D-2026-0021; every bound excerpt declares "The unit does not rely on this source for any figure it does not state here"). Repair: bind who-air-2024 (it is in the course's owner-confirmed verified replacement set, currently tagged Units 3/6) in sources/unit-01.md with a bound excerpt under sources/texts/ and add it to the U1-01 coverage row, or reword the sentence to rest on a bound source.

Misattributed figure: the 2-billion water-stress number. topic-03.mdx:112-113 states "The WHO's figure of over 2 billion people living in water-stressed countries (WHO, 2023)", and sources/unit-01.md:17 binds this to who-climate-2023 ("topic-03.mdx U1-06 (water stress figure)"). Verified by direct fetch on 2026-09-23: the WHO Climate change fact sheet (12 Oct 2023) contains no water-stress statement at all; its only water figure is "2 billion people lack safe drinking water". The water-stress figure belongs to the WHO Drinking-water fact sheet (13 Sep 2023): "In 2021, over 2 billion people live in water-stressed countries". The bound excerpt's own note (sources/texts/who-climate-2023.md:22-25) asserts a "water-stress key fact" that is not on the page, so the excerpt misdescribes its source. Repair: re-bind the claim to who-water-2023 (fetch, excerpt under sources/texts/, sources row, U1-06 coverage row) and correct the who-climate-2023 excerpt note, or replace the claim with a figure the climate fact sheet actually states.

Unsupported superlative about the Indus Delta mangroves. topic-03.mdx:50-51: "the mangrove creeks of the Indus Delta, which is one of the largest arid-zone mangrove forests in the world" - uncited, and not supported by the bound source: the abbas2012 abstract (verified in full via the publisher, isprs-archives.copernicus.org, fetch 2026-09-23) states "The Indus delta region contains the world's fifth-largest mangrove forest" and describes the coastline's "typical arid subtropical climate" separately, making no arid-zone ranking. The bound excerpt truncates exactly at "The Indus delta region contains the world's ..." and its support note does not list this claim. Repair: reword to the sourced ranking with the existing citation (e.g. "...the mangrove creeks of the Indus Delta, which holds the world's fifth-largest mangrove forest (Abbas et al., 2012)") or bind a source that supports the arid-zone characterisation.

Teacher-notes cross-reference inaccuracy. unit-teacher-notes.mdx:21-23: "the Keenjhar Lake from 1.3 returns as a resource rate in 1.3 and a practicum option in 1.4". Topic 1.4 contains no Keenjhar practicum option (its practicum task is the two-bin classroom trial; Keenjhar appears in 1.4 only in the opening classroom situation), and "returns ... in 1.3" is self-referential. Repair: reword to match the actual content, e.g. "...returns in 1.3's resource-rate debate and in 1.4's opening situation".

Assessment construction notes (no key conflicts): the MCQ key is heavily skewed to option b (7 of 10 correct answers are b; d is never correct), which weakens the bank against pattern-guessing - consider redistributing correct options in a future revision. MCQ-10 reuses topic-04's worked example verbatim (one large tin instead of twelve packets), making its Apply label generous (closer to Remember), and RRQ-10's two-part answer is given nearly verbatim in topic-04's misconception text, making its Analyze label generous. Bloom bands as authored still honour the spec (check:bloom-bands exit 0).

Bare-URL link text in all four topics' ## Further reading sections (topic-01.mdx:165-168, topic-02.mdx:163-168, topic-03.mdx:182-194, topic-04.mdx:140-145): the link text is the raw URL, so a screen-reader user hears the URL instead of a description (flagged as advisory by render-inspect on every topic). Consider descriptive link text at the next revision.

Course-level inconsistency (outside unit prose): docs/semester-1/gnas-301/course-overview.mdx:5 carries credit_hours "3 (3-0)" while catalog/courses.json and the approved content-spec carry "3 (2-1)", and content-spec.md:45-46 states the (2-1) split "is recorded here and in course-overview.mdx". The overview is an explicit "Coming soon" placeholder, so this presumably resolves when the overview is authored; flagging so the authoring pass uses the catalogue split.

Manifest under-binds the un-restoration excerpt (tooling observation for the owner, not a content defect): scripts/lib/review-evidence.mjs citedKeysFor (lines 300-312) only recognises citation keys containing a four-digit year, so the year-less key "un-restoration" never matches and specs/content/gnas-301/sources/texts/un-restoration.md is excluded from the bound input set even though the unit cites it. The file is committed at HEAD (be80907) with a clean working tree, was read and verified for this review, but a post-review edit to it would not invalidate this report. Recommend extending the key pattern or giving the key a year suffix so the excerpt is digest-bound.

Paraphrase precision: topic-02.mdx:67-69 renders the UN Decade statement as "there has never been a more urgent need to restore damaged ecosystems (UN, 2021)" where the bound excerpt reads "There has never been a more urgent need to revive damaged ecosystems than now". Presented without quotation marks, so acceptable as a paraphrase (and "restoration" is the Decade's own term), but quoting the excerpt verbatim or matching its verb would be tighter.
